Refit program loadings on a common (union) gene panel

union_panel_loadings.Rd

When each cell type selected its own features (e.g. `features = "variable"`), the per-cell-type loading matrices live on different gene sets and cannot be compared across cell types. This helper takes the union of the fitted gene panels and, for each cell type, regresses the union-panel expression on that cell type's program scores by least squares. The fits and scores are not modified: this is route B of ROADMAP item C5 (the `genes_after` arm of the model-selection benchmark showed that fitting on the union panel from the start, route A, does not improve recovery). Genes a cell type did not select get a least-squares loading on its programs instead of being missing; for the genes a cell type did fit, the refit loadings are close to (but not identical to) the flashier posterior means, which are shrunk.

Usage

union_panel_loadings(fit, genes = NULL)

Arguments

fit

A canonicalized `cell_program_fit`.

genes

Optional character vector restricting the panel; default is the union of the per-cell-type fitted genes. Genes absent from a cell type's pseudobulk get `NA` loadings there, as do genes that are degenerate (zero-variance after centering) in that cell type when scaling.

Value

A list with `loadings`, a named list of gene x program matrices on the common panel (one per cell type, 0 columns for skipped cell types), and `genes`, the panel used.

Details

The fit's preprocessing is replayed on the panel before the regression: covariate residualization (residualize mode) or removal of the fitted covariate part (fixed mode), then the recorded centering/scaling.
